title: Boot Block - boot issue with primary EFI
shortDescription: BIOS could not load the EFI boot file.
fullDescription:
HP laptops blink the Caps Lock LED in patterns to indicate hardware faults. 6-blink + 0-blink (60A) means a primary EFI boot block error — BIOS image not found or corrupted.

Use the HP BIOS recovery procedure (Win+B) to restore from the recovery partition.

fixSteps.title: BIOS recovery (Win+B)
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, hold Windows + B, press power for 1 second, release power but keep holding Win+B until recovery starts.

fixSteps.title: Recovery via USB
fixSteps.instruction: Download HP SoftPaq for your model, extract BIOS file to USB root, plug in, repeat Win+B.

whenToCallPro: If recovery doesn't trigger after multiple tries.

faq.a: No, only the BIOS firmware is restored.

title: Battery / charging system error
shortDescription: Battery validation or charging circuit fault.
fullDescription: 60B blink indicates a battery management or charging system error. Battery is not communicating, has failed authentication, or charge IC has failed.

fixSteps.title: Use HP-branded battery
fixSteps.instruction: Replace counterfeit battery with genuine HP part matching SKU.

fixSteps.title: Reset battery
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect battery and AC, hold power 30 seconds, reconnect.

fixSteps.title: Service motherboard
fixSteps.instruction: If new battery doesn't help, charging IC may need board-level repair.

faq.a: Compare SKU on label to HP parts list.

title: CPU initialization failure
fullDescription: 60C blink (6 long, 12 short, or specific HP pattern) indicates the CPU did not respond during early POST. Often related to BGA solder issues or extreme overheating damage.

fixSteps.title: Hard reset
fixSteps.instruction: Drain power and try minimum config.

title: Motherboard / system board failure
fullDescription: 60D pattern indicates general motherboard failure — chipset, VRM, or board-level fault that cannot be isolated to a single component.

fixSteps.title: Disconnect peripherals
fixSteps.instruction: Remove battery, SSD, RAM and try AC only.

title: Memory module failure
shortDescription: RAM not detected or failed POST test.
fullDescription: 60E pattern means BIOS could not initialize RAM. Modules are missing, mismatched, or failed.

fixSteps.title: Reseat RAM
fixSteps.instruction: Open RAM door, reseat both modules.

fixSteps.title: Test single sticks
fixSteps.instruction: Boot one stick at a time to identify the bad one.

title: Graphics / GPU failure
fullDescription: 60F pattern indicates GPU failure — discrete or integrated. External display test confirms GPU vs. panel issue.

fixSteps.title: External monitor test
fixSteps.instruction: Connect to TV/monitor via HDMI to confirm.

alternativeCodes: The system has detected that a cooling fan is not operating correctly
title: System fan not operating correctly
fullDescription: HP shows '90B' or 'System fan' message on screen at boot when the cooling fan does not reach minimum RPM. Unlike Lenovo, HP usually allows skipping with F2/F10 but will throttle CPU.

fixSteps.title: Compressed air clean
fixSteps.instruction: Blow through vents while holding fan to prevent overspeed.

fixSteps.title: Replace fan
fixSteps.instruction: Open laptop, replace fan/heatsink with matching FRU, reapply thermal paste.

whenToCallPro: If unfamiliar with thermal paste application.

faq.a: Yes with F2 but risk overheating.

title: Hard disk SMART error
fullDescription: Error 501 from HP HW Diagnostics indicates SMART self-test failure on the primary drive. Backup data and replace drive.

fixSteps.title: Backup data
fixSteps.instruction: Copy data immediately via Linux live USB or external SATA enclosure.

fixSteps.title: Replace drive
fixSteps.instruction: Install new SSD and reinstall Windows.

whenToCallPro: For data recovery from failing drive.

title: Hard disk Quick Test failed
fullDescription: 303 from HP UEFI diagnostics indicates a Quick Test failure on the primary drive — usually bad sectors detected during scanning.

fixSteps.title: Run Extensive test
fixSteps.instruction: Run HP Extensive Test for full surface scan.

alternativeCodes: Battery storage capacity is very low
title: Primary battery internal storage low
shortDescription: Battery has lost most of its capacity.
fullDescription: Code 601 from HP Battery Check shows the battery's storage capacity has dropped below the threshold (often <50% of design). System still works on AC but will not run long on battery.

fixSteps.title: Calibrate battery
fixSteps.instruction: Run HP battery calibration in BIOS or HP Support Assistant.

fixSteps.title: Replace battery
fixSteps.instruction: Order OEM HP battery for your model.

whenToCallPro: If battery is internal and you're not comfortable opening.

faq.a: Slightly, but won't restore worn cells.

title: Wireless device not found
shortDescription: Wi-Fi card not detected by Windows or BIOS.
fullDescription: Common HP laptop issue where Wi-Fi disappears from Device Manager. Often caused by power saving suspend, driver corruption, or hardware switch toggled off.

fixSteps.title: Toggle airplane mode
fixSteps.instruction: Press Fn+F12 (or model-specific) and check Airplane mode.

fixSteps.title: Reinstall driver
fixSteps.instruction: Uninstall Wi-Fi driver in Device Manager, reboot to reinstall, or download from HP support.

fixSteps.title: Replace M.2 Wi-Fi card
fixSteps.instruction: If still undetected, replace the M.2 2230 Wi-Fi/BT card.

videoSearchQuery: HP laptop Wi-Fi not detected fix

faq.a: Older HP business laptops have BIOS whitelists.

title: CMOS checksum error - defaults loaded
shortDescription: BIOS settings lost — CMOS battery dead.
fullDescription: CMOS checksum error appears when the BIOS configuration cannot be verified. Usually means the coin-cell RTC battery is depleted, BIOS settings reset to defaults, time/date wrong.

fixSteps.title: Set time and save defaults
fixSteps.instruction: Enter BIOS, set correct time, save and exit.

fixSteps.title: Replace coin cell
fixSteps.instruction: Open laptop, locate CR2032 (often wired with connector), replace.

whenToCallPro: If laptop is hard to disassemble.
